dispositions.codex_claim: Designed no-real outcome eligible; (3,-3pi/4) read as (3,3pi/4) gross 3, one net deduction, 2/3; decision flips canonical.
dispositions.evidence: work/nam-8227-nsscas-2026/workbench/work-orders/WB8227-principal-inverse.md:90 (MR03 line, byte-equal to shared work_order_line and to subject-rules.md:67 operational text: 'No-solution exclusion means a misread removes a solution the canonical question has; a designed no-real-solution outcome remains eligible'), :96 (D4 designed-outcome section), exemplars/WB8227-principal-inverse.md:57, trig-model-design.json recipes[1].branches[0].misread_eligibility_notes, trig-d4-fixtures.json:1585. Old clause '(including making the task easier or leaving no solution)' is gone from all three WOs. Own sympy: canonical (3,-3pi/4): -3pi/4<-pi/2, forced candidate -sqrt2/6 with asin = -pi/4 != -3pi/4 -> no real solution. Misread (3,3pi/4): 3pi/4>pi/2, forced sqrt2/6, asin = pi/4 -> no real solution. Same object (decide solvability), same comparison demand, same difficulty -> eligible. Criterion by criterion: P-B1 (bound pi/2 applied to the learner's target, F.T.) 1, P-M1 (out-of-range comparison method on misread data, judged as usual) 1, P-A1 (supported no-real conclusion, F.T.) 1; gross 3; first earned A/B on theta = P-B1 -> net 2/3. Canonical marking of the same script would give 0/3 (no actual-target comparison), so MR treatment is the lenient, OD-6-consistent outcome.
dispositions.residual: none in scope; the learner's misread answer ('no real solution') coincides with the canonical answer and still loses one mark, which is what OD-6/Cambridge MR-1 prescribe.
